concept: Index build commit quorum (commitQuorum and setIndexCommitQuorum)
summary: Source-anchored research for Index build commit quorum (commitQuorum and setIndexCommitQuorum). Run status: COMPLETED.

facts.text: For an active build, db.runCommand({setIndexCommitQuorum: "invoices", indexNames: ["invoices_1", "status_1"], commitQuorum: "majority"}) changes the threshold. indexNames must contain the complete index-name set from the original builder operation. (low confidence)

At creation, commitQuorum:0 disables quorum voting and waiting while members still start building simultaneously. A build started with zero cannot later have its quorum changed using setIndexCommitQuorum. (medium confidence)

Nodes with buildIndexes: false cannot participate in commit quorum. If a voting node has that setting, the default votingMembers quorum is unavailable; configure index building or choose another quorum. (high confidence)

An excluded or slower secondary may stall oplog application at commitIndexBuild until its local build finishes. Reducing quorum trades primary completion latency against this replication-lag risk. (medium confidence)

The driver index-management specification requires a client-side error when commitQuorum is explicitly supplied against a pre-4.4 server. Its rationale identifies MongoDB 4.2.0–4.2.5 accepting the option because of SERVER-47193, so successful parsing is not proof of supported behavior. (low confidence)

A missing required voter can leave an index build waiting rather than reject it. Percona reproduced this with one unavailable secondary in a three-member replica set; majority allowed completion with the two available members. (medium confidence)
Reaching quorum does not guarantee successful creation: the primary still checks remaining index constraints and emits abortIndexBuild on failure rather than commitIndexBuild. (low confidence)

commitQuorum controls the readiness threshold, including the primary, before a simultaneous index build commits. The default votingMembers requires all data-bearing voting members; lowering the threshold does not select which members start building. (high confidence)

Commit quorum and write concern govern different stages. The former gates primary commit readiness; MongoDB 8.0 changed the latter to acknowledge replication of the index-build oplog entry, whereas earlier releases waited for the requested nodes to finish building. (medium confidence)

SERVER-56976 records a bug where a waiting build ignored setIndexCommitQuorum updates, including after an incomplete rolling build left one secondary with an existing index. The ticket lists fixes in 4.4.7, 5.0.0-rc0 and 5.1.0-rc0. (low confidence) (verified as of 2023-10-29)

FerretDB's versioned v1.24 compatibility matrix marks setIndexCommitQuorum unsupported. MongoDB-protocol compatibility therefore does not by itself establish support for this command; this finding is limited to that versioned matrix. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-02-07)

The MongoDB development-branch design describes primary-driven index builds for which commit quorum does not apply. This branch description does not establish availability or defaults in a released server version. (low confidence)

An unavailable data-bearing voting member can leave a valid default-quorum build waiting. Percona's three-member experiment showed the build completing after the unavailable member returned; waiting alone is not evidence of command rejection. (medium confidence)

commitQuorum belongs at command level in createIndexes alongside indexes; mongosh db.collection.createIndexes(keyPatterns, options, commitQuorum) exposes it as a separate argument. (medium confidence)

Commit quorum readiness and write concern acknowledgment serve different purposes; satisfying quorum alone does not establish durability or guarantee every secondary's index is ready. (high confidence)
